summary: Yui Suzuki specializes in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum, and held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuishin Ito (1931–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He served as associate professor at Bukkyo University (1961–1997) and president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (1997).

Yujiro Motora (1858–1912) worked in philosophy and other fields, having studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885. He held posts at the Tokyo University of Education (ca. 1888–1898) and the University of Tokyo (ca. 1888–1912).
Yujun Endo (1939–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served at Taisho University as an associate professor (attested 1991) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2014).
Yuka Otani is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She held positions as a part-time lecturer at both Ryukoku University and Hanazono University (attested 2015).

Yukei Matsunaga (1929–2023) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University, and held positions at Koyasan University, serving as director in 1983, and Shuchiin University.
Yuki Takatsukasa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a doctoral student at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama (1931–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as an overseas researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn, and served as associate professor (attested 1996) and professor emeritus (attested 2015) at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College.
Yukihisa Yamao (1935–2021) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from ca. 1953 to 1961 and held a post there from ca. 1968 to 2001.

Yukimasa Mizutani (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University. He served as associate professor (ca. 1960–1974) and president (ca. 1979–1989) at Bukkyo University, later leading Bukkyo Kyoiku Gakuen and Tokai Gakuen.

Yukio Kotani (1931–) worked in Buddhist studies and other fields, studying under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served at Rissho University from ca. 1974 to 2002 as emeritus professor of comparative literature.

Yukio Sakamoto (1899–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura, Daito Shimaji, and Nichien Fukami. He held posts at Toyo University and Rissho University, where he served as dean and president.

Yukio Takeda (1934–2021) was a historian who studied at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1953–1962). He held posts at Hokkaido University, Nagoya City University, the University of Tokyo (ca. 1977–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (ca. 2000–2005).

Yukio Yamanaka is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied as a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).
Yuko Kamishima (1971–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo, was a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She held associate professor and professor posts at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2021).
Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2010).
